summary: This script launches a Docker container running the markitdown tool to convert documents to Markdown. It mounts your current directory into the container as a workspace, sets up strict security restrictions (read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities, unprivileged user), and passes along any arguments you give the script to the markitdown command inside the container.

explanations.5: These are bash safety flags: -e exits on errors, -u errors on undefined variables, and -o pipefail catches failures in command pipelines.
explanations.7: exec replaces the current shell process with docker, so when the container exits, the script exits too without spawning an extra process.
explanations.8: This mounts your current working directory into the container at /workspace with caching enabled for performance.
explanations.9: Makes the entire container filesystem read-only so the tool can't modify system files, only temp directories we explicitly allow.
explanations.10: Creates a temporary writable in-memory filesystem at /tmp (64MB max) where the tool can write scratch data, but with noexec and nosuid flags to prevent executing code there.
explanations.11: Similar temp filesystem at /run for the container's runtime needs.
explanations.12: Removes all Linux capabilities from the container, starting from scratch and only allowing what Docker deems safe.
explanations.13: Prevents the container from gaining new privileges (like escalating to root), even if a vulnerability is exploited.
explanations.14: Runs the container as the current user (your UID and group ID) instead of root, so any files created have your ownership.
